objective: Replace the coarse one-active-Quest-v2 constraint with a two-axis quest model: multiple non-terminal OPEN quests may coexist, while exactly one quest at most owns player execution FOCUS. Preserve current quest continuity, evidence, rewards, anti-farming, timing, derived-state authority and dynamic next-action selection.

roles_before.artifact: Quest v2 creation is rejected while any other Quest v2 quest is ACTIVE.
ACTIVE is the non-terminal lifecycle state; COMPLETED/CANCELLED/FAILED/EXPIRED are terminal.
The sole active Quest v2 quest implicitly owns the PWA/controller execution focus.
The existing Hallo Quest remains the current player task until legitimately resolved or redirected.
system-quest-difficulty:v1 outcome_key blocks duplicate active/completed scored outcomes.
Timing v2 NONE/RECOMMENDED_WINDOW/HARD_EXTERNAL and fail-closed CHALLENGE semantics remain authoritative.
Neon system_events remains the single mutable owner of derived RPG state.
System chooses the highest-value feasible next execution target from authoritative current context rather than blindly following a fixed queue.
Base SHA preserves the complete pre-change single-active behavior.

role_dispositions.destination: Multiple Quest v2 quests may remain OPEN/ACTIVE; creation no longer consumes a global active slot.
ACTIVE continues to mean non-terminal/open for backward compatibility; terminal lifecycle and objective/evidence gates stay unchanged.
A separate ledger-derived focus axis selects at most one OPEN Quest v2 as FOCUSED; other OPEN quests are BACKGROUND. Legacy ledgers with no focus event infer the earliest open Quest v2 as focus.
The existing Hallo Quest remains the inferred focus without rewriting historical player events.
Outcome-key duplicate prevention remains unchanged and applies independently of focus/background state.
Timing semantics and deadline consequences remain unchanged for every OPEN quest.
Focus changes are append-only system_events; no second state owner or mutable mirror is introduced.
When focus is absent or legitimately reconsidered, controller re-evaluates current context; background OPEN quests do not automatically steal focus.
Recorded base SHA remains the rollback point; migration is additive/superseding and does not rewrite historical events.

capability_probes.assertion: Existing Quest v2 lifecycle, objectives, progress, completion, cancellation, failure and expiration still work while more than one Quest v2 is OPEN.
Creating or retaining several OPEN quests never makes several quests player-facing focus at once; latest valid explicit focus wins and invalid/terminal targets cannot be focused.
Creating a new background OPEN quest cannot silently replace the currently focused quest.
A pre-migration ledger with exactly one OPEN Quest v2 and no focus events projects that quest as focused without adding or rewriting ledger events.
Two scored quests with the same protected outcome_key still cannot coexist or double-reward merely because multiple OPEN quests are now allowed.
Recommended windows remain non-terminal and hard external deadlines retain existing expiration behavior for focused and background OPEN quests.
Recorded base SHA reconstructs the former one-active-Quest-v2 behavior and full prior runtime.

tests.expected: Memory projection allows multiple OPEN Quest v2 records, maintains one focus, rejects focus to missing/terminal/non-v2 targets, and preserves legacy implicit focus.
Migration 009 removes the single-active creation gate, validates quest.focus through system_apply_action and keeps one ledger-derived focus selection.
Quest lifecycle, timing, outcome identity, resolution, projection and action-gate suites pass.
Architecture/continuity/controller guards pass with the new focus contract.
Player home panel renders the explicitly projected focused quest rather than the first arbitrary OPEN quest.
